exactText:
Yesterday we did a livestream. TL;DR:

We have set internal goals of having an automated AI research intern by September of 2026 running on hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and a true automated AI researcher by March of 2028. We may totally fail at this goal, but given the extraordinary potential impacts we think it is in the public interest to be transparent about this.
sourceQuote: an automated AI research intern by September of 2026 running on hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and a true automated AI researcher by March of 2028
normalizedClaim: OpenAI achieves an automated AI research intern by September 2026 and a true automated AI researcher by March 2028.
resolutionCriteria: OpenAI public announcements, blog posts, or technical reports confirming deployment of systems meeting the described internal goals (automated research intern / full automated researcher).

exactText: 2025 has seen the arrival of agents that can do real cognitive work; writing computer code will never be the same. 2026 will likely see the arrival of systems that can figure out novel insights. 2027 may see the arrival of robots that can do tasks in the real world.
sourceQuote: 2026 will likely see the arrival of systems that can figure out novel insights. 2027 may see the arrival of robots that can do tasks in the real world.
normalizedClaim: Systems capable of figuring out novel insights arrive in 2026; robots capable of real-world tasks arrive in 2027.
resolutionCriteria: Public demonstrations or peer-reviewed publications of AI systems generating novel scientific insights in 2026, and commercial/research robots performing useful real-world physical tasks in 2027.

exactText: On our current trajectory, we believe we may be only a couple of years away from early versions of true superintelligence. By the end of 2028, more of the world’s intellectual capacity could reside inside of data centres than outside.
sourceQuote: we may be only a couple of years away from early versions of true superintelligence. By the end of 2028, more of the world’s intellectual capacity could reside inside of data centres than outside.
normalizedClaim: Early versions of true superintelligence arrive within a couple of years of February 2026; by end of 2028 more of the world’s intellectual capacity resides in data centers than outside them.
resolutionCriteria: OpenAI or peer-lab announcements of systems exceeding human-level performance across most cognitive domains by ~2028, plus quantitative estimates (e.g., FLOPs or effective researcher-equivalents) showing data-center capacity exceeding human intellectual capacity.

exactText: The OpenAI CEO says the company is “not quite yet” at AGI, but expects to have an internal system he would call AGI by the end of 2026.
sourceQuote: expects to have an internal system he would call AGI by the end of 2026
normalizedClaim: OpenAI has an internal system that Sam Altman would call AGI by the end of 2026.
resolutionCriteria: OpenAI public statement, TIME interview follow-up, or technical report confirming an internal system meeting Altman’s/OpenAI’s definition of AGI by 2026-12-31.

exactText: Intelligence too cheap to meter is well within grasp. This may sound crazy to say, but if we told you back in 2020 we were going to be where we are today, it probably sounded more crazy than our current predictions about 2030.
sourceQuote: Intelligence too cheap to meter is well within grasp.
normalizedClaim: Intelligence (AI inference/compute) becomes too cheap to meter (approaching marginal cost of electricity) within the 2020s–early 2030s timeframe referenced.
resolutionCriteria: Industry reports or OpenAI/pricing data showing AI inference costs approaching the cost of electricity (near-zero marginal cost per token beyond energy) by ~2030.

exactText: I would certainly say by the end of this decade, so, by 2030, if we don’t have models that are extraordinarily capable and do things that we ourselves cannot do, I’d be very surprised.
sourceQuote: by the end of this decade, so, by 2030, if we don’t have models that are extraordinarily capable and do things that we ourselves cannot do, I’d be very surprised
normalizedClaim: By the end of 2030, AI models exist that are extraordinarily capable and can do things humans cannot do.
resolutionCriteria: Publicly demonstrated or peer-reviewed AI systems performing tasks (e.g., novel scientific discovery) beyond current human capability by 2030-12-31.

exactText: In 2026 we expect that our AI systems may be able to make small new discoveries; in 2028 we could be looking at big ones.
sourceQuote: In 2026 we expect that our AI systems may be able to make small new discoveries; in 2028 we could be looking at big ones.
normalizedClaim: OpenAI AI systems make small new scientific discoveries in 2026 and larger ones by 2028.
resolutionCriteria: OpenAI publications, blog posts, or peer-reviewed papers attributing novel scientific discoveries (small in 2026, significant in 2028) to their AI systems.

exactText: In ten more years, I believe we are almost certain to build superintelligence.
sourceQuote: In ten more years, I believe we are almost certain to build superintelligence.
normalizedClaim: OpenAI / humanity builds superintelligence by approximately 2035.
resolutionCriteria: Widely accepted demonstration or declaration by major labs of systems exceeding human intelligence across essentially all domains by 2035.

exactText: 2025 has seen the arrival of agents that can do real cognitive work; writing computer code will never be the same.
sourceQuote: 2025 has seen the arrival of agents that can do real cognitive work
normalizedClaim: AI agents capable of real cognitive work arrive in 2025.
resolutionCriteria: Widespread commercial deployment and use of AI agents performing substantive cognitive tasks (coding, research, multi-step workflows) in 2025, as evidenced by product launches from OpenAI, Microsoft, Anthropic, Google, etc.

resolution.explanation: Multiple major labs launched and scaled agentic systems capable of real cognitive work (coding agents, research agents, multi-step tool-using agents) throughout 2025.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Gentle Singularity (contemporaneous claim) and subsequent 2025 product launches

exactText: We are now, like, in the singularity. ... Now we're actually in the moment that we used to talk about at the lunch table in a very not-serious way. I've been waiting for this my whole life, and I think it's going to be incredible, hugely positive, awesome for the world.
sourceQuote: We are now, like, in the singularity.
normalizedClaim: Humanity is currently in the technological singularity as of mid-2026.
resolutionCriteria: Consensus among AI researchers / major labs or quantitative metrics (recursive self-improvement rate, capability acceleration) confirming the singularity threshold has been crossed; otherwise remains a contested claim.
imputationNote: Definition of 'singularity' is contested; treated as a take with a one-year review horizon for whether the claim gains broad acceptance.
